rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so the first experiment should explore a promising multimodal configuration. Config_004 uses multimodal processing with transformer aggregation (potentially capturing complex interactions) and concat fusion, which could yield higher accuracy. It balances complexity with cost, using imagenet_vit_l (strong image encoder) and pca_n2000 (moderate RNA encoder). This tests the hypothesis that multimodal approaches with transformer aggregation are effective, while keeping costs manageable compared to more expensive alternatives.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal configurations with transformer aggregation and concat fusion (like config_004) achieve moderate accuracy (0.5988). This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder (pca_n2000 → scgpt) while keeping the image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) and aggregation method unchanged. scgpt is a more advanced RNA encoder, and this change could improve accuracy without increasing complexity. The expected cost is similar to config_004 (≈5 GPU hours), balancing exploration of a key design choice with computational efficiency.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal configurations with scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, and concat fusion (config_004) achieve the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests changing the fusion method to weighted, which may improve performance by allowing more nuanced interaction between modalities. The expected cost is similar to config_004 (around 4.76 GPU hours), balancing exploration of a key design choice with cost efficiency.

The existing evidence shows config_004 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.5988). This experiment tests replacing the image encoder with resnet50 (cheaper and potentially more efficient) while keeping the same aggregation (transformer) and fusion (concat) methods. This clarifies whether the image encoder choice impacts performance and balances exploration of cheaper architectures with exploitation of the current best configuration's design.

Existing evidence shows config_004 (transformer aggregation, concat fusion) achieves the highest accuracy (0.5988). This experiment tests avgpool aggregation with weighted fusion using scgpt and imagenet_vit_l, which could reveal if alternative aggregation/fusion combinations improve accuracy. It balances exploration of key design choices (aggregation/fusion) while using a similar encoder setup to config_004, keeping costs lower than transformer-based models.

Existing evidence shows config_004 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, transformer aggregation, concat fusion) achieves the highest accuracy (0.5988). This experiment tests replacing the image encoder with resnet50 and switching fusion to weighted, which could improve performance while maintaining the effective transformer aggregation. The expected cost is higher than config_004 (approx 7-8 GPU hours) but offers a promising trade-off between exploration and exploitation, as resnet50 might capture complementary features with weighted fusion.

The existing evidence shows config_004 (multimodal, scgpt RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, transformer aggregation, concat fusion) achieves the highest accuracy (0.5988). This experiment tests replacing transformer aggregation with avgpool (simpler, cheaper) while keeping other components identical. It clarifies if aggregation method impacts performance and offers a lower-cost alternative. Expected cost: ~3.5 GPU hours (avgpool is less complex than transformer).

The existing evidence shows that config_004 (multimodal, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) achieves the highest accuracy (0.5988) so far. This experiment tests a similar setup but with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, which could clarify if RNA encoder choice significantly impacts performance. It balances exploration (testing a new RNA encoder) with exploitation (maintaining the effective multimodal, transformer, and concat setup). The expected cost is similar to config_004 (around 4.76 GPU hours), ensuring efficient use of remaining budget.

The existing evidence shows config_048 (72.07% accuracy) is the best so far using scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l with transformer aggregation and concat fusion. This experiment tests the same RNA/image encoders but with weighted fusion instead of concat, which could improve accuracy. It clarifies whether fusion method impacts performance while keeping cost similar (estimated ~4.65 GPU hours). This balances exploitation of proven components with exploration of a key design choice.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with imagenet_vit_l image encoder (config_031: 72.5% accuracy) and transformer aggregation perform best. This experiment tests scvi_n200 with resnet50 image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion, which could potentially improve accuracy by leveraging resnet50's features. It balances exploration of image encoder alternatives with the proven effectiveness of scvi_n200, while keeping cost manageable (estimated ~8-9 GPU hours).
